# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 9 (Bi-Vb Np9)
**ID:** Bi-Vb Np9
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 9
**Title (English, from literature):** Exchanging designated collective property that was asked for
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-np9

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dutiyagaṇikacetāpana-sikkhāpada* ("Exchanging designated collective property that was asked for") is the ninth rule in the *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* (relinquishment and confession) chapter of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule provides that if a nun solicits a collective requisite that has been designated for a specific communal purpose and subsequently exchanges it for something else, she incurs an offense requiring her to relinquish the obtained item and confess [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the text has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Full parallels to this rule are preserved across several Vinaya lineages, including the Pali *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Np 9) and *Parivāra* (Np 9), as well as corresponding rules in the Dharmaguptaka (*Nissaggiya Pācittiya* 23), Mahīśāsaka (Np 28), Sarvāstivāda (Np 28), and Chinese and Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda traditions (Np 28) [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus reflects extensive formulaic overlap within the Pali Vinaya, sharing the most extensive segments with adjacent Bhikkhunī rules addressing the reallocation and exchange of funds or requisites (*Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya* 7, 10, 6, and 8) as well as various *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* rules (such as Bu-Vb Np 6, 7, 26, 28, and 29) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects matches with a Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* text and multiple Tibetan canonical and commentarial Vinaya works, including the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-2) and Vinaya treatises such as the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) and *Vinayakārikā* (D4123) [DharmaNexus].
